result.topic_en: The page ends tables of linear relations among the sums q and p for orders m+n=7 and m+n=8, then begins a 'third method' that writes the double series ∑(1/z^n)(1+1/2^m+…+1/(z−1)^m) in terms of y and z.
result.transcription:
168 MEDITATIONES CIRCA
Pro ordine $m+n=7$
$q+q^6=p+p^7$ | $q+q^2+q^3+q^4+q^5+q^6=2p^2+2p^4+2p^6+p-p^7$
$-1 \quad -2$
$q^2+q^5=p^2+p^7$ | $q^2+2q^3+3q^4+4q^5+5q^6=2p^2+6p^4+10p^6-p^2+p^7$
$-1 \quad -5 \quad -10$
$q^3+q^4=p^3+p^7$ | $q^3+3q^4+5q^5+10q^6=6p^4+20p^6+p^3-p^7$
$-1 \quad +4 \quad -10 \quad -2 \quad -20$
Pro ordine $m+n=8$
$q+q^7=p+p^8$ | $q+q^2+q^3+q^4+q^5+q^6+q^7=2p^2+2p^4+2p^6+p-p^8$
$+1$
$q^2+q^6=p^2+p^8$ | $q^2+2q^3+3q^4+4q^5+5q^6+6q^7=2p^2+6p^4+10p^6-p^2+p^8$
$+1 \quad +6 \quad +2$
$q^3+q^5=p^3+p^8$ | $q^3+3q^4+6q^5+10q^6+15q^7=6p^4+20p^6+p^3-p^8$
$+1 \quad +5 \quad +15 \quad +10$
$2q^4=p^4+p^8$ | $q^4+4q^5+10q^6\ 20q^7=2p^4+20p^6-p^4+p^8$
$+1 \quad +4 \quad +10 \quad +20 \quad +2 \quad +20$
hoc ergo modo iſtas aequationes quousque lubuerit facile continuare licet.
Tertia Methodus
ad huiusmodi ſeries perueniendi.
26. Haec methodus ſimilis fere eſt praecedenti, conſidero enim ſeriem
$\int\frac{1}{z^n}\left(1+\frac{1}{2^m}+\frac{1}{3^m}+\ldots\ldots+\frac{1}{(z-1)^m}\right)$,
cuius valor modo ſuperiori expreſſus eſt
$=\int\frac{1}{z^n}\left(\frac{1}{y^m}\right)-\int\frac{1}{z^{m+n}}$
modo

items.quote: hoc ergo modo iſtas aequationes quousque lubuerit facile continuare licet.
items.english: In this way, therefore, one may easily continue these equations as far as one pleases.
